name: Sanya Phoenix International Airport
before:
The airport for Sanya on Hainan, China's tropical beach destination, about 15 km north west of the city. It is the twenty fourth busiest in the country and second on the island behind Haikou.

It is built for size. The runway is around 3,400 metres by 60 metres and takes a fully loaded 747 or A340, on a site of close to ten thousand acres.

High speed rail sits right next door. Sanya Phoenix Airport station on the Hainan Western Ring line opened in December 2015 and connects to Sanya Railway Station on the Eastern Ring line 10 km away, putting both coasts of the island within easy reach without a car.

The Russian market is the one to watch here. This was the first airport in Hainan to take a transcontinental flight, when Transaero flew non-stop from Moscow in 2007, and since 2017 IrAero, Alrosa and Azur Air have all flown in from Russian cities.
after:
The airport for Sanya on Hainan, about 15 km north west of the city. In 2025 it was the 24th busiest in China and second on the island behind Haikou.

The airport is built for size: the runway is around 3,400 metres and takes a fully loaded 747 and other large aircraft.

High speed rail sits right next door. Sanya Phoenix Airport station on the Hainan Western Ring line connects to Sanya Railway Station on the Eastern Ring line, putting both coasts of the island within easy reach without a car.

Russia is the market to watch here: the airport lists routes to Moscow, Novosibirsk, Irkutsk and Vladivostok, among other Russian cities.

claims.claim: the airport lists routes to Moscow, Novosibirsk, Irkutsk and Vladivostok, among other Russian cities
claims.inAfter: the airport lists routes to Moscow, Novosibirsk, Irkutsk and Vladivostok, among other Russian cities
claims.note: Replaces 'since 2017 IrAero, Alrosa and Azur Air have all flown in from Russian cities', which nothing current confirms. The operator's live route list names Moscow (莫斯科), Novosibirsk (新西伯利亚), Irkutsk (伊尔库茨克) and Vladivostok (海参崴), and also Khabarovsk, Yekaterinburg, Kazan, St Petersburg, Ufa, Krasnoyarsk and Ulan-Ude: eleven Russian cities, the largest group among its international routes. Its introduction counts 36 international and regional routes at 30 June 2026. Attributed, as it is the airport's own list; Wikipedia's current revision also describes Russian airlines flying in from various Russian cities.
